name: TLS & Certificates
description: Crypto exposure: client and server TLS choices, certificate hygiene, and JA4 fingerprints used to spot malware C2 traffic blending in with regular HTTPS.

charts.title: JA4 Client Fingerprints
charts.description: Distribution of TLS clients by JA4 fingerprint. Rare or unique fingerprints in your environment frequently belong to malware, RAT or research-tooling rather than legitimate browsers.

charts.title: Suspected Malware Fingerprints
charts.description: Direct hits against the threat-category list (CobaltStrike, Emotet, Metasploit, …). Any non-empty value here is critical and worth a manual review of the matching flow.

charts.title: TLS Versions in Use
charts.description: Server-selected TLS versions across observed handshakes. Anything below TLS 1.2 (e.g. TLS 1.0, 1.1, SSLv3) indicates obsolete crypto and downgrade-attack exposure.

charts.title: Server-Selected Cipher Suites
charts.description: Cipher suites chosen by servers. Concentration of weak ciphers (RC4, 3DES, NULL, EXPORT) means servers in your estate accept downgraded encryption.

charts.title: Self-Signed Certificates
charts.description: Share of certificates that are self-signed. A meaningful share indicates dev/test infrastructure, MITM proxies, or attacker-operated infra leaking into production traffic.

charts.title: Certificate Signature Algorithms
charts.description: Distribution of certificate signature algorithms. MD5 / SHA-1 signatures are deprecated; their presence indicates outdated PKI or rogue certificate authorities.
